booklet.title: The site operations over REST and MCP
booklet.author: Giovanni Porcari

purpose.p: How a program or an agent works on Kajenn Press sites through the 53 site operations, the same ones the administration and Help me use: how to call them, what each needs, and what it answers.

list.item: A websites installation with site sources; capabilities says which parts are configured (sites, publishing, rendering) and lists the operations.
A bearer token of an identity with the editor tag and grants on the sites (read, write, create_site, build, publish).

step.title: Call an operation
step.p: Every operation is a route of one application on the websites root, reachable two ways with the same arguments:

list.item: REST: POST /<operation> with a JSON object of arguments.
MCP: POST /mcp, JSON-RPC tools/call with name the operation and arguments the same object; tools/list lists them.

step.p: Both answer {"ok": true, "result": …} or {"ok": false, "error": {"code", "message", …}}. Over REST the error codes map to HTTP statuses: unauthenticated 401, forbidden 403, not_found 404, conflict 409, unavailable 503, any other 422.

step.title: Hold the site while changing it
step.p: Changes go to the caller's working copy of the site and need its editing lock: site_open takes the site (force takes it from another holder), site_save writes the working copy as a new S3 version of the source, site_close releases it. The lock expires after 30 minutes without changes.

Every change carries an idempotency key chosen by the caller: repeating a call with the same key and the same arguments returns the first result without running it again; the same key with other arguments is refused. Keys are kept 24 hours.

step.title: The operations
step.p: Every operation except site_list, starters_list, site_new and site_import also takes site_id. "Lock" says whether the caller must hold the site; "Key" whether the call takes an idempotency key.

rule.why: A repeated call is recognised by its key.

rules.rule: Use a new key for every distinct change and the same key when retrying it.

rule.why: Other holders' changes are lost when a site is taken.

rules.rule: Save before closing or leaving a site for long.

rule.why: The plan names exactly what changed and what is wrong.

limits.limit: One holder edits a site at a time; there is no merge of concurrent changes.

facts.fact: The operations are the union of READS, CHANGES, CONTROLS, LIBRARY, PUBLISHING and SERVERS: 53, each a route of PressApplication (tests/site/test_site_service.py).
REST maps unauthenticated, forbidden, not_found, conflict, unavailable to 401, 403, 404, 409, 503 and other errors to 422.
REST calls are POST /<operation>; MCP calls are JSON-RPC tools/call on /mcp.
The editing lock expires after 30 minutes.
